title: Estimated Judge Reliabilities for Weighted Bradley-Terry-Luce Are Not Reliable

problem.claim: Learning latent scales for subjective properties requires human-labeled data, which is costly and time-consuming to obtain.

narrative_sequence.summary: Applications seek latent scales for subjective properties such as photo excitement and font legibility, but obtaining human-labeled data is costly and time-consuming.

Pairwise comparisons are widely used to acquire labels because they reduce the effect of biases and can work effectively outside controlled environments, despite quadratic cost in the number of items.

source_observation.claim: Pairwise comparisons are used for subjective labeling because they generally reduce bias effects and support data collection outside controlled environments.

interpretation.claim: A labeling method may be preferred for robustness to bias and deployment flexibility even when its data-collection cost scales quadratically with the number of items.

application.claim: When designing subjective-labeling workflows, consider pairwise comparisons where bias mitigation and uncontrolled-environment usability are important.

exception.claim: Pairwise comparisons incur quadratic cost in the number of items.

unknowns: The abstract units do not state the paper's specific method or theoretical result.
